verdict.headline: The bond selloff runs into a second day and the long bond reaches its 2007 high
verdict.label: Premarket: S&P 500 futures -0.6%, Nasdaq 100 -1.0%, Dow -0.3%; 10Y 5.139%, 30Y 5.438%, 2Y 4.897%; Brent $104.19; gold futures $4,293; BTC ~$84,300; JGB 10Y 3.08%. US-China truce extended to January 10. Costco reports after the close.
verdict.rationale_short:
The long end kept selling overnight after Wednesday's PMI-led repricing. The thirty-year rose another 3 basis points to 5.438%, within a basis point of its 2007 high of 5.44%, the ten-year reached 5.139%, its highest since July 2007, and the two-year 4.897%, its highest since 2023. New York Fed President Williams called another increase this year "reasonable" without committing to October, a second official after Barr, with CME FedWatch near 73% for October 28. Brent rose a second day to $104.19 and Japan's ten-year added 10 basis points to 3.08% on Tokyo's reopening, so the selling is global rather than a US auction story.

The night's constructive news did not help. Treasury Secretary Bessent said the US-China truce is extended two months to January 10, removing the November deadline the semiconductor group was carrying, and Nasdaq 100 futures still fell 1% against 0.6% for the S&P 500. This morning the discount rate matters more to equities than trade policy does.

The levels that would change the picture: a thirty-year close above 5.44% sets a two-decade high while Treasury's buyback program is still buying that maturity; a close back under 5.35% would put Wednesday's move down to one survey and a weak auction. Friday's core PCE is the first hard inflation data since the repricing.
verdict.lede_short: The bond selloff ran into a second day: the thirty-year reached 5.438%, a basis point from its 2007 high, and the ten-year 5.139% as a second Fed official called another hike reasonable. The US-China truce was extended to January 10, yet Nasdaq futures fell 1%, the most of any index — rates, not trade policy, are setting prices. A long-bond close above 5.44% or Friday's PCE decides whether the move holds.

supporting_data.label: Nasdaq 100 futures fell 1%, S&P 500 futures 0.6% and Dow futures 0.3%, with the thirty-year at 5.438% and the two-year at 4.897%, its highest since 2023 — the heaviest selling is in the longest-duration index, which is what a rates move rather than a growth scare produces
The ten-year touched 5.139%, its highest since July 2007 — a second day higher after the largest one-day rise since April 2025, so the move is extending rather than fading

New York Fed President Williams called another rate increase this year 'reasonable' but did not commit to October — a second voter after Barr describing a further hike as the default, with CME FedWatch near 73% for October 28

Bessent said the US-China trade truce, due to lapse in November, is extended two months to January 10 as Xi began his state visit — a deadline removed from the quarter, yet chip-heavy futures are still the weakest
Brent rose 1.1% to $104.19 by 4:01 a.m. ET as prospects for a quick US-Iran breakthrough faded — a second day higher takes back most of the September decline the long end had been counting on
Japan's ten-year rose 10 basis points to 3.08% as Tokyo reopened after five closed sessions — the selling is global, so a US-only explanation such as the five-year auction is not enough on its own

watchlist_mentions.note: The truce extension to January 10 removes the November deadline from the China policy track, and Huang is expected at tonight's state dinner. Futures say rates are outweighing that: Nasdaq 100 futures are down 1% on a night of constructive trade news.
Rose 5.00% to $1,096.16 on Wednesday's down day, six sessions before its September 30 fiscal fourth quarter. The highest-momentum AI name opens into a duration-led Nasdaq decline.

trade_setups.thesis: The long bond has risen for a second session to 5.438%, within a basis point of the 2007 high, on a hot PMI, a poorly received five-year auction, two Fed officials leaning toward another increase and Brent back above $104. Treasury's expanded buyback program is buying that maturity through November 4, so a new high would be set against an official bid.
trade_setups.entry: Thirty-year 5.438% against the 5.44% 2007 high; ten-year 5.139%. Seven-year auction today; August core PCE Friday.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close above 5.44% confirms a two-decade high in term premium. A close back under 5.35% puts Wednesday's move down to one survey and a weak auction.

trade_setups.thesis: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose more than 8% during Tokyo's five-day holiday and the truce extension removed the group's main policy deadline, yet Nasdaq 100 futures are the weakest index. The relative move against the Nasdaq 100 today separates a rates-driven decline from positioning coming out of a crowded trade.
trade_setups.entry: Nasdaq 100 futures -1.0%; Micron $1,096.16 after a 5.00% gain on Wednesday; Micron reports September 30.
trade_setups.invalidation: Chips falling in line with long-duration growth says rates. Chips falling notably more on a day policy risk eased says positioning.

trade_setups.thesis: The repricing so far rests on a survey. Costco after the close is the first large consumer read at a 5.1% ten-year, and core PCE on Friday is the first hard inflation data since.
trade_setups.entry: Costco consensus near $94.87 billion revenue and $6.52 EPS; October hike odds near 73% on CME FedWatch.
trade_setups.invalidation: A firm consumer print and a firm core PCE make the repricing durable. Soft readings leave roughly 73% October odds resting on one survey and a weak auction.
